messages:
Maya: Quick ask — I'm drafting a concise customer-facing SOP for tenant priming and surge-proofing. Need a short checklist we can share in kickoff calls and in-runbooks (aim for 6 bullets max).

Jorge: Love it. High-level items I'd include: 1) Warm pools + duration, 2) Session pooling TTL, 3) Lightweight prefix caching, 4) Burst routing policy, 5) Observability knobs, 6) Rollback triggers. Keep language non-technical for customers.

Anika: +1. Add one line on renewal signal: if weekly success rate drops < 90% for 3 days escalate to AM.

Maya: Nice — can you help wording for "warm pools" so it's customer friendly?

Jorge: Sure — "Warm pool: we keep a small set of pre-initialized workers for your account so cold-start latency stays low during early traffic. Typical size: 1-3 workers for small accounts, 5+ for high QPS."

Anika: Also call out cheap priming requests — suggest customers send 1-3 synthetic queries after a deploy to keep KV cache hot. Example wording: "Run two short seed queries (takes < 5s) to make responses faster for early users."

Sam: SRE note — include a snippet for streaming timeouts to avoid hung client sockets. Recommend: server idle 30s, client keepalive 15s. Something like:
```
streaming: 
  server_idle_timeout: 30s
  client_keepalive: 15s
```

Maya: Oof good call. We should also recommend batching guidance for shared-rate accounts (to reduce token cost): batch window 50-200ms, but if latency SLO < 300ms prefer window 50ms.

Jorge: Add a short "what to expect" table so customers know tradeoffs:
- Lower cost: larger batching windows (100-200ms)
- Lower latency: smaller windows (10-50ms) + warm pool
- Highest reliability: multi-region routing + fallback model tier

Anika: For renewal-risk capture, suggest adding a single survey hook after 2 weeks: "Is the response relevance meeting your expectations?" link -> CS ticket if negative. Keeps it simple.

Maya: Drafting now. Proposed 6-bullet customer SOP (plain language):
1) "Warm pool sizing": we pre-start a few workers for faster first responses. Start with 2 and scale to 5 for high traffic.
2) "Seed queries": run 1-3 quick example prompts after deploy to prime caches.
3) "Batching tradeoffs": bundling requests lowers cost but adds 50-200ms; pick smaller windows if you need snappy UX.
4) "Streaming & timeouts": keep client keepalives on every 15s and expect server idle cut after 30s.
5) "Surge fallback": enable automatic model fallback (lower-tier) to maintain availability during spikes.
6) "Health check & renewals": we'll ping a short feedback question at week 2; sustained drops in success will trigger an AM outreach.

ops-bot: Document created: https://redwood.internal/docs/cs/tenant-priming-sop (ops tag: cs/sop) :white_check_mark:

Sam: Tiny tweak — wording for #5: "If you enable graceful fallback, some responses may be from a smaller model during extreme load; we surface this in logs."

Maya: Good. I'll bake that in and send to templates. Thanks team — I'll paste final SOP into the customer kickoff slide and the runbook. :thumbsup:

Jorge: Can you add a one-liner for support engineers: how to toggle warm pool size? E.g., `PUT /v1/tenants/{id}/config {"warm_pool":3}`

Maya: Yup. I'll add the API example in the engineer-facing appendix but keep customer-facing doc high level.

Anika: If you want, I can run a short enablement session with field ops next week to walk through the checklist.

Maya: Please do — scheduling poll incoming.
